Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => reflexivity x; compose := fun x y z f g => transitivity g f |}  (a preorder as a thin category: hom x y is inhabited exactly when x ≤ y, and all parallel arrows are identified)

statement_record.book: A symmetric monoidal structure on a preorder (X,≤) is a unit I ∈ X and a product ⊗ : X×X → X with (a) monotonicity: x1≤y1 and x2≤y2 imply x1⊗x2 ≤ y1⊗y2; (b) I⊗x = x = x⊗I; (c) (x⊗y)⊗z = x⊗(y⊗z); (d) x⊗y = y⊗x, where (b),(c),(d) are STRICT equalities of elements, so no coherence data is carried; the package (X,≤,I,⊗) is a symmetric monoidal preorder, and dropping (d) leaves a monoidal preorder.
statement_record.intree: Class Monoidal (I, the bifunctor tensor : C ∏ C ⟶ C, unit_left/unit_right/tensor_assoc as isomorphisms, plus triangle and pentagon), Class StrictMonoidal (strict_assoc_obj / strict_unit_left_obj / strict_unit_right_obj as OBJECT equalities with the structural isos the transported identities), Class SymmetricMonoidal (braid with braid_invol and both hexagons), over a base category which may be Proset P (hom x y := R x y, all parallel arrows identified).

evidence.intree_statement: Inductive CTerm : list Colour -> list Colour -> Type := | CT_id (cs : list Colour) : CTerm cs cs | CT_braid (cs ds : list Colour) : CTerm (cs ++ ds) (ds ++ cs) | CT_comp {cs ds es} : CTerm ds es -> CTerm cs ds -> CTerm cs es | CT_tens {cs1 ds1 cs2 ds2} : CTerm cs1 ds1 -> CTerm cs2 ds2 -> CTerm (cs1 ++ cs2) (ds1 ++ ds2) | CT_gen {cs ds} : S cs ds -> CTerm cs ds  — a formal wiring diagram: left/right boundaries are LISTS OF LABELLED WIRES, generators are the boxes, CT_tens stacks wires in parallel (concatenation), CT_braid is the crossing icon, CT_id the bare wire, and CT_nothing := CT_id [] (line 181) the absence of wires

Class ColouredPROP : Type := { cprop_cat : Category; cprop_strict : @StrictMonoidal cprop_cat; cprop_symmetric : @SymmetricMonoidal cprop_cat; ...; cprop_of_list : list Colour -> @obj cprop_cat; cprop_unit_nil : @I cprop_cat (strict_is_monoidal cprop_strict) = cprop_of_list nil; cprop_tensor_app : forall (cs ds : list Colour), ((cprop_of_list cs) ⨂ (cprop_of_list ds))%object = cprop_of_list (cs ++ ds) }  — exactly the book's two conventions, as STRICT object equalities: a stack of labelled wires denotes the monoidal product of its labels, and no wires denotes the unit

Fixpoint cinterp {cs ds : list Colour} (t : CTerm S cs ds) : ⟦cs⟧ ~{P}~> ⟦ds⟧ := match t with | CT_id _ => id | CT_braid cs ds => cbraid_hom cs ds | CT_comp g f => cinterp g ∘ cinterp f | CT_tens f g => cinterp f ⊞c cinterp g | CT_gen g => v _ _ g end  — the semantic content of validity: a diagram with input wires cs and output wires ds denotes a morphism from the tensor of the input labels to the tensor of the output labels (over a thin base, exactly the inequality ⊗cs ≤ ⊗ds)

statement_record.book: Over a monoidal preorder (X,≤,I,⊗): a wiring diagram has parallel wires on the left and on the right, each labelled by an element of X, with a box between them; parallel wires labelled x and y denote x ⊗ y (in either bracketing), a wire labelled I and the total absence of wires both denote I, and the diagram is VALID iff the monoidal product of the left labels is ≤ the monoidal product of the right labels (so the box x → y is valid iff x ≤ y). Boxes, wires and crossings are the icons of the notation.
statement_record.intree: Inductive CTerm S : list Colour -> list Colour -> Type (boxes = CT_gen, wire = CT_id, crossing = CT_braid, parallel = CT_tens by list concatenation, series = CT_comp), with the label-fold conventions as the ColouredPROP fields cprop_unit_nil : I = cprop_of_list nil and cprop_tensor_app : cprop_of_list cs ⨂ cprop_of_list ds = cprop_of_list (cs ++ ds), and cinterp t : ⟦cs⟧ ~> ⟦ds⟧ giving the assertion a diagram makes. The non-strict variant of the fold is Definition tensor_list xs := fold_right (⨂) I xs with tfold_app : tfold (Γ ++ Δ) ≅ tfold Γ ⨂ tfold Δ (Theory/Multicategory/Representable.v:55,67,113).
statement_record.strength_comparison: in-tree-stronger in that diagrams are formal, machine-checked syntax with a semantics (not a notational convention), and the two label conventions hold as strict object equalities; in-tree-WEAKER on the item's defining clause: 'valid' is never defined, and the book's biconditional (diagram valid IFF one inequality holds) is not stated — in-tree a diagram is a proof-relevant term that PRODUCES a morphism, with no thin/preorder base where morphism-existence collapses to the inequality.

gap: Three precise gaps. (1) No validity predicate and no biconditional: nothing states 'the diagram with inputs cs and outputs ds is valid iff ⊗cs ≤ ⊗ds'; over a general (non-thin) base that biconditional is false, and no thin instantiation of CTerm/ColouredPROP exists (the only thin monoidal category in-tree, _2, is never used as a PROP). (2) The in-tree language is inherently SYMMETRIC — CT_braid is a constructor and cprop_symmetric a field — whereas the book defines wiring diagrams over a not-necessarily-symmetric monoidal preorder and counts the crossing as an extra icon licensed only by axiom (d); there is no planar/crossing-free fragment. (3) Wires labelled I are not identified with absent wires at the level of diagrams: cprop_unit_nil identifies the empty LIST with I, but a colour whose object is I is not proved interchangeable with the empty list.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition CInterpF : CFreeCat S ⟶ P  (with Definition CInterpF_Strict (line 436) : StrictMonoidalFunctor ... and Definition CInterpF_Symmetric (line 568) : @SymmetricMonoidalFunctor (CFreeCat S) P (CFreeCat_Symmetric S Cdec) (cprop_symmetric P) CInterpF)  — soundness of the graphical calculus: a valuation of the interior boxes extends along every diagram to a strict symmetric monoidal functor, so the assertion the exterior box makes follows from the assertions the interior boxes make

Fixpoint cinterp {cs ds : list Colour} (t : CTerm S cs ds) : ⟦cs⟧ ~{P}~> ⟦ds⟧ := match t with | CT_id _ => id | CT_braid cs ds => cbraid_hom cs ds | CT_comp g f => cinterp g ∘ cinterp f | CT_tens f g => cinterp f ⊞c cinterp g | CT_gen g => v _ _ g end  (with Definition CValuation : Type := ∀ cs ds, S cs ds → (⟦cs⟧ ~{P}~> ⟦ds⟧), line 845)  — the book's slice-by-slice construction, one clause per rule: CT_tens is the monotonicity step, CT_comp the transitivity step, CT_id reflexivity, CT_braid the symmetry step, CT_gen the interior-box hypothesis

Theorem cinterp_unique : ∀ cs ds (t : CTerm S cs ds), fmap[G] t ≈ hom_cast (eq_sym (Hobj cs)) (eq_sym (Hobj ds)) (cinterp P S v t)  — the graphical reading is the ONLY one: any strict symmetric monoidal G agreeing with the valuation on generators agrees with the diagram interpretation on every diagram

Program Instance hom_preorder {C : Category} : PreOrder (@hom C) := { PreOrder_Reflexive := fun _ => id; PreOrder_Transitive := fun _ _ _ f g => g ∘ f }  — the exact correspondence the construction rests on: reflexivity is the bare wire (id) and transitivity is wiring boxes in series (composition)

statement_record.book: Over a monoidal preorder X, a wiring diagram is read as a proof: each box with left side x and right side y asserts x ≤ y, and a diagram of interior boxes wired inside an exterior box asserts the implication 'if all interior assertions hold then the exterior assertion holds'. The encoded proof is obtained by taking successive vertical slices — each slice one inequality justified by monotonicity applied to the boxes and identity wires it cuts — and chaining the slices by transitivity; reflexivity licenses a bare wire, and a crossing-free diagram needs no appeal to symmetry.
statement_record.intree: cinterp turns any diagram (CTerm) into a morphism ⟦cs⟧ ~> ⟦ds⟧ from a CValuation of the generators, by exactly the book's clauses (tensor = monotonicity, composition = transitivity, identity = reflexivity, braid = symmetry); CInterpF packages it as a strict symmetric monoidal functor CFreeCat S ⟶ P (soundness) and cinterp_unique pins it uniquely; hom_preorder records that a category's hom relation is a preorder with id for reflexivity and ∘ for transitivity.
statement_record.strength_comparison: in-tree-stronger in generality and rigour (the construction is a machine-checked functor into an ARBITRARY strict symmetric monoidal target, with a uniqueness theorem, rather than an informal reading), but in-tree-weaker on the item's specific reading: the target is required to be a coloured PROP (strict symmetric monoidal with a list-of-labels object correspondence) and is never a preorder, so 'a diagram proves an inequality from inequalities' is never stated; the slice/transitivity structure appears only as the recursion of cinterp, not as a soundness statement about chains of ≤.

gap: (1) No thin/preorder instantiation: the graphical-proof reading over a monoidal preorder (where a morphism IS the inequality, so the diagram literally proves an implication between inequalities) is never stated — the machinery is exercised only over genuine (proof-relevant) PROPs.
